_comment: Every file the add-on needs, grouped by where it comes from, because that is the order you do the work in:
open one link, follow one guide, drop that group's files in. Paths are relative to the folder holding mgs4.exe.
tools/install_checks.ps1 reads this and tools/mgs4_dlss.ps1 renders it, as the Setup tab and as --report.
Versions match the 'setup this was verified on' table in README.md - change both together.
required   a missing file here is a failure rather than a note
url        where this group's files come from; shown as a button above the group
guide      one or two sentences on what to do with them
files[].path    relative to the game folder - this is the row's label
files[].detail  the line under it; files[].url only when that one file comes from somewhere else

sections.title: The game
sections.blurb: Everything else goes in the folder this sits in.
sections.guide: Metal Gear Solid 4, Master Collection Vol. 2. In its options set Graphics -> API to DirectX 12, FXAA off, vsync off and the frame limiter to 60.

files.detail: one line containing 2492670; lets `mgs4.exe --stage` boot without bouncing through Steam

sections.title: ReShade, with add-on support
sections.blurb: The host this add-on loads into. The plain build looks identical on disk and silently loads nothing.
sections.guide: Run the ReShade setup, pick mgs4.exe and the Direct3D 10/11/12 renderer, and choose the build WITH full add-on support. It installs itself as dxgi.dll next to the game.

files.detail: ReShade itself, under the name the game loads

sections.title: This add-on
sections.blurb: The DLSS add-on and the settings it reads.
sections.guide: Unzip the release and copy both files next to mgs4.exe. Building from source instead: dlss-addon\build.bat, then sh dlss-addon/install.sh.

files.detail: its settings; the first run writes the detected InternalRes into it

sections.title: DLSS runtime
sections.blurb: The NVIDIA runtime that does the upscaling.
sections.guide: Copy lib/Windows_x86_64/rel/nvngx_dlss.dll from the SDK next to mgs4.exe. If the NVIDIA app's DLSS override is on for this game it supplies the runtime instead and no file is needed here.

sections.title: DLSS 5 Neural Rendering
sections.blurb: Optional. With these present the add-on runs DLAA on the final image, so NR works at full strength.
sections.guide: Both files come from the RenoDX Discord, under Pinned Messages. Copy them next to mgs4.exe; the add-on detects renodx-dlss5.addon64 on its own and moves the DLAA pass to the composite. nvngx_dlssnr.dll can also come from the NVIDIA app.

sections.title: Frame generation
sections.blurb: Optional, and only useful above 60 Hz. Needs FrameGen set in the Settings tab.
sections.guide: Copy these out of bin/x64 in the Streamline release (2.12 or newer) next to mgs4.exe. The last one is NVIDIA's frame-generation runtime and comes from the DLSS SDK or the NVIDIA app instead.

files.detail: the Streamline entry point the add-on loads

sections.title: Frame limiter
sections.blurb: Optional. The port is built around 60 fps; this is what holds it there.
sections.guide: Needs an ASI loader: put winmm.dll next to mgs4.exe (the game imports winmm at startup, so that is what loads the scripts folder), then the .asi and its ini in scripts\ with TargetFrameRate = 60.

files.detail: Ultimate ASI Loader, which loads everything in scripts\

sections.title: Fallbacks
sections.blurb: Only needed on a build without the in-game DirectX 12 option.
sections.guide: Skip this unless Options -> Graphics has no DirectX 12 entry. The ASI forces the D3D12 backend; with the in-game option available, leave scripts\MGS4_D3D12.ini at Enabled = 0.

files.detail: forces the D3D12 backend when the game cannot be asked for it
